item.title: POLICE LOG
item.description: The Port Townsend Police Department (PTPD) reported a total of 174 calls from Jan. 30 to Feb. 5. PTPD conducted 46 traffic stops, and responded to nine welfare checks, five traffic collisions, four reports of harassment, six reports of suspicious activity and five trespassing calls during that week. Calls such as domestic violence and suicides are left out of the […] The post POLICE LOG first appeared on Port Townsend & Jefferson County Leader.

item.title: Teen airlifted after hitting semi on Hood Canal Bridge
item.description: Early morning drivers were subjected to a mile-long backup in both directions along SR 104 after a Feb. 13 crash on the Hood Canal Bridge. Just before 2 a.m., 18-year-old Cyler Williamson-Roberts of Port Hadlock was driving westbound in a silver 2003 Volkswagen Jetta, when he crossed the center line and struck a semi head-on. item.title: BRIEFS
item.description: Vendor applications Vendor applications for the 2026 Jefferson County Fair are now open. With somewhere between 8,000 to 10,000 visitors over three days in August, the fair offers vendors an opportunity to connect with the community and showcase products, services and talents. item.title: Port Hadlock driver may face homicide charge after fatal Highway 101 crash
item.description: A man died in a head-on crash on U.S. Highway 101 near Sequim on Feb. 15. The crash occurred near milepost 267 at around 7 p.m. and blocked the highway for several hours. item.title: Voters approve school bond, fire district levies
item.description: With 54% voter turnout as of Feb. 12, the Port Townsend School District (PTSD) bond and both East Jefferson Fire Rescue (EJFR) levy lid lifts passed, with at least 70% of ballots cast in each measure’s favor. Certified official results will be available on Feb. 20. item.title: Commissioners back Beaver Valley transfer station site
item.description: Jefferson County commissioners unanimously voted Feb. 9 to advance the Beaver Valley site at state routes 19 and 104 for a new transfer station. item.title: Snow drought worsens on Peninsula
item.description: Now in the midpoint of winter, snowpack in the Olympic Mountains continues to weaken with federal data revealing the basin’s snow water equivalent at just 34% of median as of Feb. 1, a level of snowpack that climatologists said may result in one of the most challenging snow seasons in recent memory. The measurement is included in the most recent […] The post Snow drought worsens on Peninsula first appeared on Port Townsend & Jefferson County Leader.

item.title: Two airlifted after explosion; fire sinks sailboat in Glen Cove
item.description: An explosion and subsequent fire aboard a 50-foot sailboat near Port Townsend is under investigation by the Jefferson County Fire Marshall.
